correctness.rationale: For n=d−1, the derivative Laurent power spectrum is supported on [−n,n], a complete set of distinct residues modulo 2d−1. Its nth coefficient is q_n times the conjugate of q_0, so a competitor must have both derivative endpoint coefficients nonzero. Multiplying the common Laurent polynomial by z^n gives the product of a spectral factor and its reversed conjugate; on the admissible locus the 2n roots are distinct reciprocal-conjugate pairs. Every competitor thus chooses exactly one root from each pair. The leading-modulus change for a flip is the product of the flipped root moduli; the constant-modulus ratio is its inverse. The real polynomial equations saying a nonempty subset has modulus product one are proper in ordered root coordinates and give null sets in coefficient charts. At d=3 the nearest alias of frequency 1 is −4, outside [−3,3], and the separation only increases with d; the zeroth moment is also unaliased. After fixing the competitor phase, equality of the first moment solves for the competitor constant as αx+β. For a wrong flip |α| differs from one, so the energy equation is an actual circle equation (possibly empty or a point). For no flip the first moment forces the same constant. Locally continuous root labelings give measurable exceptional sets, and Fubini makes their planar-null sections jointly null. The argument includes nongeneric competitors, assumes indexed grid data, and does not extend the nonaliasing argument to d=2.
